speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अरोषणो यः समलोष्ट काञ्चनः
प्रहीण शोको गतसन्धि विग्रहः ।
निन्दा प्रशंसोपरतः प्रियाप्रिये
चरन्नुदासीनवदेष भिक्षुकः ॥
iast:
aroṣaṇo yaḥ samaloṣṭa kāñcanaḥ
prahīṇa śoko gatasandhi vigrahaḥ |
nindā praśaṃsoparataḥ priyāpriye
carannudāsīnavadeṣa bhikṣukaḥ ||
english: One who is free of anger, to whom a clod and gold are the same, who has left grief behind, is beyond alliance and conflict, has stopped caring for blame and praise, and moves among the pleasant and unpleasant as if indifferent: this is a mendicant.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नीवार मूलेङ्गुद शाकवृत्तिः
सुसंयतात्माग्निकार्येष्वचोद्यः ।
वने वसन्नतिथिष्वप्रमत्तो
धुरन्धरः पुण्यकृदेष तापसः ॥
iast:
nīvāra mūleṅguda śākavṛttiḥ
susaṃyatātmāgnikāryeṣvacodyaḥ |
vane vasannatithiṣvapramatto
dhurandharaḥ puṇyakṛdeṣa tāpasaḥ ||
english: Living on wild rice, roots, ingudi nuts and greens, well self-controlled, needing no urging in the fire rites, living in the forest and attentive to guests: this foremost doer of good is an ascetic.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अपकृत्वा बुद्धिमतो दूरस्थोऽस्मीति नाश्वसेत् ।
दीर्घौ बुद्धिमतो बाहू याभ्यां हिंसति हिंसितः ॥
iast:
apakṛtvā buddhimato dūrastho'smīti nāśvaset |
dīrghau buddhimato bāhū yābhyāṃ hiṃsati hiṃsitaḥ ||
english: Having wronged a wise person, one should not relax, thinking 'I am far away'. The arms of the wise are long; with them, the one who was harmed strikes back.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न विश्वसेदविश्वस्ते विश्वस्ते नातिविश्वसेत् ।
विश्वासाद्भयमुत्पन्नं मूलान्यपि निकृन्तति ॥
iast:
na viśvasedaviśvaste viśvaste nātiviśvaset |
viśvāsādbhayamutpannaṃ mūlānyapi nikṛntati ||
english: Do not trust one who is not trustworthy, and do not trust too much one who is. Danger that arises from trust cuts away even the roots.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनीर्ष्युर्गुप्तदारः स्यात्संविभागी प्रियंवदः ।
श्लक्ष्णो मधुरवाक्स्त्रीणां न चासां वशगो भवेत् ॥
iast:
anīrṣyurguptadāraḥ syātsaṃvibhāgī priyaṃvadaḥ |
ślakṣṇo madhuravākstrīṇāṃ na cāsāṃ vaśago bhavet ||
english: One should be free of jealousy, guard one's wife, share with others, speak kindly, be gentle and sweet-spoken to women, but not come under their control.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पूजनीया महाभागाः पुण्याश्च गृहदीप्तयः ।
स्त्रियः श्रियो गृहस्योक्तास्तस्माद्रक्ष्या विशेषतः ॥
iast:
pūjanīyā mahābhāgāḥ puṇyāśca gṛhadīptayaḥ |
striyaḥ śriyo gṛhasyoktāstasmādrakṣyā viśeṣataḥ ||
english: Women are worthy of honour, greatly blessed, pure and the light of the house. They are called the fortune of the home; so they should be protected above all.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पितुरन्तःपुरं दद्यान्मातुर्दद्यान्महानसम् ।
गोषु चात्मसमं दद्यात्स्वयमेव कृषिं व्रजेत् ।
भृत्यैर्वणिज्याचारं च पुत्रैः सेवेत ब्राह्मणान् ॥
iast:
piturantaḥpuraṃ dadyānmāturdadyānmahānasam |
goṣu cātmasamaṃ dadyātsvayameva kṛṣiṃ vrajet |
bhṛtyairvaṇijyācāraṃ ca putraiḥ seveta brāhmaṇān ||
english: Give the inner apartments to your father, give the kitchen to your mother, give the cattle to one like yourself, and go to the farming yourself. Carry on trade through servants, and serve brahmins through your sons.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अद्भ्योऽग्निर्ब्रह्मतः क्षत्रमश्मनो लोहमुत्थितम् ।
तेषां सर्वत्रगं तेजः स्वासु योनिषु शाम्यति ॥
iast:
adbhyo'gnirbrahmataḥ kṣatramaśmano lohamutthitam |
teṣāṃ sarvatragaṃ tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati ||
english: Fire arose from water, the kshatriya from the brahmin, iron from stone. Their power reaches everywhere, but it is quenched in its own source.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नित्यं सन्तः कुले जाताः पावकोपम तेजसः ।
क्षमावन्तो निराकाराः काष्ठेऽग्निरिव शेरते ॥
iast:
nityaṃ santaḥ kule jātāḥ pāvakopama tejasaḥ |
kṣamāvanto nirākārāḥ kāṣṭhe'gniriva śerate ||
english: The good, born in noble families, with energy like fire, always forbearing and showing no outward sign, lie quiet like fire in wood.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यस्य मन्त्रं न जानन्ति बाह्याश्चाभ्यन्तराश् च ये ।
स राजा सर्वतश्चक्षुश्चिरमैश्वर्यमश्नुते ॥
iast:
yasya mantraṃ na jānanti bāhyāścābhyantarāś ca ye |
sa rājā sarvataścakṣuściramaiśvaryamaśnute ||
english: The king whose counsel is not known by those outside or those inside, and who has eyes everywhere, enjoys sovereignty for a long time.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
करिष्यन्न प्रभाषेत कृतान्येव च दर्शयेत् ।
धर्मकामार्थ कार्याणि तथा मन्त्रो न भिद्यते ॥
iast:
kariṣyanna prabhāṣeta kṛtānyeva ca darśayet |
dharmakāmārtha kāryāṇi tathā mantro na bhidyate ||
english: When about to act, do not announce it; show only what has been done. In tasks of dharma, desire and wealth, in this way counsel is not leaked.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
गिरिपृष्ठमुपारुह्य प्रासादं वा रहोगतः ।
अरण्ये निःशलाके वा तत्र मन्त्रो विधीयते ॥
iast:
giripṛṣṭhamupāruhya prāsādaṃ vā rahogataḥ |
araṇye niḥśalāke vā tatra mantro vidhīyate ||
english: Climbing to a mountain top or a palace roof, having gone to a secluded place, or in a forest without bushes: there counsel should be held.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नासुहृत्परमं मन्त्रं भारतार्हति वेदितुम् ।
अपण्डितो वापि सुहृत्पण्डितो वाप्यनात्मवान् ।
अमात्ये ह्यर्थलिप्सा च मन्त्ररक्षणमेव च ॥
iast:
nāsuhṛtparamaṃ mantraṃ bhāratārhati veditum |
apaṇḍito vāpi suhṛtpaṇḍito vāpyanātmavān |
amātye hyarthalipsā ca mantrarakṣaṇameva ca ||
english: One who is not a friend does not deserve to know one's highest counsel, Bharata; nor does a friend who is unwise, nor a wise one who lacks self-control. Choose a minister only after testing him, for on him depend gaining wealth and keeping counsel.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
कृतानि सर्वकार्याणि यस्य वा पार्षदा विदुः ।
गूढमन्त्रस्य नृपतेस्तस्य सिद्धिरसंशयम् ॥
iast:
kṛtāni sarvakāryāṇi yasya vā pārṣadā viduḥ |
gūḍhamantrasya nṛpatestasya siddhirasaṃśayam ||
english: The king whose counsel is hidden, and whose tasks his courtiers know only once they are done: his success is beyond doubt.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अप्रशस्तानि कर्माणि यो मोहादनुतिष्ठति ।
स तेषां विपरिभ्रंशे भ्रश्यते जीवितादपि ॥
iast:
apraśastāni karmāṇi yo mohādanutiṣṭhati |
sa teṣāṃ viparibhraṃśe bhraśyate jīvitādapi ||
english: One who out of delusion carries out blameworthy actions falls even from life when they go wrong.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
कर्मणां तु प्रशस्तानामनुष्ठानं सुखावहम् ।
तेषामेवाननुष्ठानं पश्चात्तापकरं महत् ॥
iast:
karmaṇāṃ tu praśastānāmanuṣṭhānaṃ sukhāvaham |
teṣāmevānanuṣṭhānaṃ paścāttāpakaraṃ mahat ||
english: Doing praiseworthy actions brings happiness; not doing them causes great remorse later.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स्थानवृद्ध क्षयज्ञस्य षाड्गुण्य विदितात्मनः ।
अनवज्ञात शीलस्य स्वाधीना पृथिवी नृप ॥
iast:
sthānavṛddha kṣayajñasya ṣāḍguṇya viditātmanaḥ |
anavajñāta śīlasya svādhīnā pṛthivī nṛpa ||
english: For one who knows standing still, growth and decline, who understands the six policies, and whose conduct is not despised, the earth is in his own control, king.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अमोघक्रोधहर्षस्य स्वयं कृत्यान्ववेक्षिणः ।
आत्मप्रत्यय कोशस्य वसुधेयं वसुन्धरा ॥
iast:
amoghakrodhaharṣasya svayaṃ kṛtyānvavekṣiṇaḥ |
ātmapratyaya kośasya vasudheyaṃ vasundharā ||
english: For one whose anger and joy are not fruitless, who personally oversees what must be done, and whose treasury is known to himself, this earth yields wealth.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नाममात्रेण तुष्येत छत्रेण च महीपतिः ।
भृत्येभ्यो विसृजेदर्थान्नैकः सर्वहरो भवेत् ॥
iast:
nāmamātreṇa tuṣyeta chatreṇa ca mahīpatiḥ |
bhṛtyebhyo visṛjedarthānnaikaḥ sarvaharo bhavet ||
english: A ruler should be content with just the name and the royal parasol. He should distribute wealth to his servants and not be the one who takes everything.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणं वेद भर्ता वेद स्त्रियं तथा ।
अमात्यं नृपतिर्वेद राजा राजानमेव च ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇaṃ veda bhartā veda striyaṃ tathā |
amātyaṃ nṛpatirveda rājā rājānameva ca ||
english: A brahmin knows a brahmin, a husband knows his wife, a king knows his minister, and a king knows a king.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न शत्रुरङ्कमापन्नो मोक्तव्यो वध्यतां गतः ।
अहताद्धि भयं तस्माज्जायते नचिरादिव ॥
iast:
na śatruraṅkamāpanno moktavyo vadhyatāṃ gataḥ |
ahatāddhi bhayaṃ tasmājjāyate nacirādiva ||
english: An enemy who has fallen into one's lap and deserves death should not be let go; for danger soon arises from one who is not killed.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
दैवतेषु च यत्नेन राजसु ब्राह्मणेषु च ।
नियन्तव्यः सदा क्रोधो वृद्धबालातुरेषु च ॥
iast:
daivateṣu ca yatnena rājasu brāhmaṇeṣu ca |
niyantavyaḥ sadā krodho vṛddhabālātureṣu ca ||
english: Anger should always be carefully restrained towards the gods, kings and brahmins, and towards the old, children and the sick.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
निरर्थं कलहं प्राज्ञो वर्जयेन्मूढ सेवितम् ।
कीर्तिं च लभते लोके न चानर्थेन युज्यते ॥
iast:
nirarthaṃ kalahaṃ prājño varjayenmūḍha sevitam |
kīrtiṃ ca labhate loke na cānarthena yujyate ||
english: The wise person should avoid pointless quarrels, which fools engage in. He gains a good name in the world and is not joined to misfortune.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
प्रसादो निष्फलो यस्य क्रोधश्चापि निरर्थकः ।
न तं भर्तारमिच्छन्ति षण्ढं पतिमिव स्त्रियः ॥
iast:
prasādo niṣphalo yasya krodhaścāpi nirarthakaḥ |
na taṃ bhartāramicchanti ṣaṇḍhaṃ patimiva striyaḥ ||
english: One whose favour bears no fruit and whose anger is also without effect: people do not want him as master, as women do not want an impotent husband.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न बुद्धिर्धनलाभाय न जाड्यमसमृद्धये ।
लोकपर्याय वृत्तान्तं प्राज्ञो जानाति नेतरः ॥
iast:
na buddhirdhanalābhāya na jāḍyamasamṛddhaye |
lokaparyāya vṛttāntaṃ prājño jānāti netaraḥ ||
english: Intelligence is not for gaining wealth, nor is dullness the cause of poverty. The wise person knows how the world turns; no one else does.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
विद्या शीलवयोवृद्धान्बुद्धिवृद्धांश्च भारत ।
धनाभिजन वृद्धांश्च नित्यं मूढोऽवमन्यते ॥
iast:
vidyā śīlavayovṛddhānbuddhivṛddhāṃśca bhārata |
dhanābhijana vṛddhāṃśca nityaṃ mūḍho'vamanyate ||
english: The fool always despises those senior in learning, character and age, those senior in intelligence, and those senior in wealth and family, Bharata.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनार्य वृत्तमप्राज्ञमसूयकमधार्मिकम् ।
अनर्थाः क्षिप्रमायान्ति वाग्दुष्टं क्रोधनं तथा ॥
iast:
anārya vṛttamaprājñamasūyakamadhārmikam |
anarthāḥ kṣipramāyānti vāgduṣṭaṃ krodhanaṃ tathā ||
english: Troubles quickly come to one of ignoble conduct, the unwise, the envious, the unrighteous, one who speaks harshly, and one who is quick to anger.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अविसंवादनं दानं समयस्याव्यतिक्रमः ।
आवर्तयन्ति भूतानि सम्यक्प्रणिहिता च वाक् ॥
iast:
avisaṃvādanaṃ dānaṃ samayasyāvyatikramaḥ |
āvartayanti bhūtāni samyakpraṇihitā ca vāk ||
english: Not deceiving, giving, not breaking an agreement, and speech well directed: these win living beings over.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अविसंवादको दक्षः कृतज्ञो मतिमानृजुः ।
अपि सङ्क्षीण कोशोऽपि लभते परिवारणम् ॥
iast:
avisaṃvādako dakṣaḥ kṛtajño matimānṛjuḥ |
api saṅkṣīṇa kośo'pi labhate parivāraṇam ||
english: One who does not deceive, is capable, grateful, intelligent and straightforward finds people around him even when his treasury is exhausted.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
धृतिः शमो दमः शौचं कारुण्यं वागनिष्ठुरा ।
मित्राणां चानभिद्रोहः सतैताः समिधः श्रियः ॥
iast:
dhṛtiḥ śamo damaḥ śaucaṃ kāruṇyaṃ vāganiṣṭhurā |
mitrāṇāṃ cānabhidrohaḥ sataitāḥ samidhaḥ śriyaḥ ||
english: Steadiness, calm, self-control, purity, compassion, speech that is not harsh, and not betraying friends: these seven are the fuel of good fortune.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
असंविभागी दुष्टात्मा कृतघ्नो निरपत्रपः ।
तादृङ्नराधमो लोके वर्जनीयो नराधिप ॥
iast:
asaṃvibhāgī duṣṭātmā kṛtaghno nirapatrapaḥ |
tādṛṅnarādhamo loke varjanīyo narādhipa ||
english: One who does not share, who is evil-minded, ungrateful and shameless: such a lowest of men should be avoided in the world, lord of men.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न स रात्रौ सुखं शेते स सर्प इव वेश्मनि ।
यः कोपयति निर्दोषं स दोषोऽभ्यन्तरं जनम् ॥
iast:
na sa rātrau sukhaṃ śete sa sarpa iva veśmani |
yaḥ kopayati nirdoṣaṃ sa doṣo'bhyantaraṃ janam ||
english: He does not sleep happily at night, as if with a snake in the house, who, being himself at fault, angers innocent people close to him.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
येषु दुष्टेषु दोषः स्याद्योगक्षेमस्य भारत ।
सदा प्रसादनं तेषां देवतानामिवाचरेत् ॥
iast:
yeṣu duṣṭeṣu doṣaḥ syādyogakṣemasya bhārata |
sadā prasādanaṃ teṣāṃ devatānāmivācaret ||
english: Those who, if offended, could harm one's welfare and security, Bharata: one should always keep them pleased, as one would the gods.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
येऽर्थाः स्त्रीषु समासक्ताः प्रथमोत्पतितेषु च ।
ये चानार्य समासक्ताः सर्वे ते संशयं गताः ॥
iast:
ye'rthāḥ strīṣu samāsaktāḥ prathamotpatiteṣu ca |
ye cānārya samāsaktāḥ sarve te saṃśayaṃ gatāḥ ||
english: Wealth entrusted to women, to those newly risen, and to the ignoble: all of it falls into doubt.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यत्र स्त्री यत्र कितवो यत्र बालोऽनुशास्ति च ।
मज्जन्ति तेऽवशा देशा नद्यामश्मप्लवा इव ॥
iast:
yatra strī yatra kitavo yatra bālo'nuśāsti ca |
majjanti te'vaśā deśā nadyāmaśmaplavā iva ||
english: Where a woman, a gambler or a child gives the orders, those lands sink helplessly, like a raft of stone in a river.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
प्रयोजनेषु ये सक्ता न विशेषेषु भारत ।
तानहं पण्डितान्मन्ये विशेषा हि प्रसङ्गिनः ॥
iast:
prayojaneṣu ye saktā na viśeṣeṣu bhārata |
tānahaṃ paṇḍitānmanye viśeṣā hi prasaṅginaḥ ||
english: Those who are attached to the main purposes, not to particulars, I consider wise, Bharata; for particulars lead to entanglement.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यं प्रशंसन्ति कितवा यं प्रशंसन्ति चारणाः ।
यं प्रशंसन्ति बन्धक्यो न स जीवति मानवः ॥
iast:
yaṃ praśaṃsanti kitavā yaṃ praśaṃsanti cāraṇāḥ |
yaṃ praśaṃsanti bandhakyo na sa jīvati mānavaḥ ||
english: The man whom gamblers praise, whom bards praise, whom loose women praise: that man does not truly live.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
हित्वा तान्परमेष्वासान्पाण्डवानमितौजसः ।
आहितं भारतैश्वर्यं त्वया दुर्योधने महत् ॥
iast:
hitvā tānparameṣvāsānpāṇḍavānamitaujasaḥ |
āhitaṃ bhārataiśvaryaṃ tvayā duryodhane mahat ||
english: Abandoning the Pandavas, great archers of boundless energy, you have placed the great sovereignty of the Bharatas in Duryodhana, Bharata.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
तं द्रक्ष्यसि परिभ्रष्टं तस्मात्त्वं नचिरादिव ।
ऐश्वर्यमदसंमूढं बलिं लोकत्रयादिव ॥
iast:
taṃ drakṣyasi paribhraṣṭaṃ tasmāttvaṃ nacirādiva |
aiśvaryamadasaṃmūḍhaṃ baliṃ lokatrayādiva ||
english: You will soon see him fallen from it, bewildered by the intoxication of power, like Bali fallen from the three worlds.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
अनीश्वरोऽयं पुरुषो भवाभवे
सूत्रप्रोता दारुमयीव योषा ।
धात्रा हि दिष्टस्य वशे किलायं
तस्माद्वद त्वं श्रवणे घृतोऽहम् ॥
iast:
anīśvaro'yaṃ puruṣo bhavābhave
sūtraprotā dārumayīva yoṣā |
dhātrā hi diṣṭasya vaśe kilāyaṃ
tasmādvada tvaṃ śravaṇe ghṛto'ham ||
english: This person is not master of his rising or falling; he is like a wooden doll moved by strings. He is under the control of what the Creator has ordained. So speak on; I am intent on listening.
